evidence.quote: No Personal Data is transferred outside the EEA by the Subprocessors listed in Annex 1.

transfer_mechanism.footnote: This is the institutional answer (DPA 10.2 is stated 'for institutional customers'). The privacy policy, which covers all accounts, says that where a subprocessor processes data outside the EU/EEA, transfers rely on safeguards such as the Standard Contractual Clauses; no such subprocessor is named.
transfer_mechanism.note: dataprivacyframework.gov not checked, since no US recipient is named.

evidence.quote: We use a small, documented set of GDPR-compliant subprocessors, each limited to a single purpose and bound by a data processing agreement.

subprocessors_public.note: Listed on kahubi.com/compliance and in DPA Annex 1.

evidence.quote: For institutional customers (invoice billing), every subprocessor is a European company processing data in the EU.
Annex 1 – Approved Subprocessors

subprocessors_count.footnote: Self-serve (card-paying) accounts add Stripe (Stripe Payments Europe Ltd, Ireland), so the compliance page lists 13 companies in total. Stripe is stated as not applicable to institutional buyers.
subprocessors_count.note: Institutional answer: 12 third-party companies in DPA Annex 1: Hostup, TensorX, GreenPT, Inceptron, Berget AI, Scaleway, Gladia, Lemonfox, Staan, Bunny, Visma, Lettermint (Berget AI counted once, though the compliance page also lists it for transcription). No group companies are listed; the self-hosted OpenPanel analytics is not a third party.

evidence.quote: No Personal Data is transferred outside the EEA by the Subprocessors listed in Annex 1.

subprocessors_non_eea.note: Per the vendor's own statement; every Annex 1 entry gives an EU location. Stripe (self-serve only) is contracted via its Irish entity; any processing beyond that is not described.

evidence.quote: shall automatically notify subscribers when it is updated

subprocessor_notice.note: At least 30 days' notice for hosting and storage providers (DPA 4.4); 14-day objection window (DPA 4.7). Changes of model version with an existing subprocessor need no notice (DPA 4.6).

evidence.quote: Last updated: October 27, 2026

evidence.quote: The AI workspace for research
Primary: TensorX (Ireland). Backup: GreenPT (Netherlands), Inceptron (Sweden), Berget AI (Sweden), Scaleway (France)
AI processing is carried out with open-source models running entirely in EU data centres

ai_providers.footnote: This is the institutional answer (DPA 10.2). The journal-editors page says a sealed review refuses non-EU AI providers 'even if your account is set up with a different one', which suggests other providers can apply to some accounts; none are named.
ai_providers.note: Third-party EU companies running open-source models; the model names and their developers are not stated.

evidence.quote: We do not use your research content to train AI models — neither our own nor third parties'.
our AI subprocessors are used via API agreements that exclude training on customer data

trains_on_content.note: Terms section 4 says the same. The privacy policy's 'improve the Service' purpose is limited to aggregate, de-identified usage analytics, not model training.

ai_zero_retention.note: No zero-data-retention statement for the AI providers in the privacy policy, compliance page, DPA or terms. The journal-editors page says the text is held in the EU model provider's memory while it works, under a DPA, but does not state the provider's retention or logging.

ai_admin_off.note: No institution control to switch off AI found. The journal-editors page describes a team owner switch that makes reviews 'sealed', which is not an AI off switch.

ai_act_statement.note: No Kahubi EU AI Act position on the compliance, privacy, terms, about pages or llms.txt. llms.txt lists general guides that discuss the AI Act, which are not a statement about Kahubi.

certifications.note: No ISO, SOC or other certificate named on the compliance page, privacy policy, DPA or llms.txt. Web search found nothing.

evidence.quote: Read our compliance & security overview
Passwords are hashed, transport is encrypted (TLS), and access to production systems is restricted.
Data is stored on GDPR-compliant, encrypted infrastructure in Sweden

encryption.note: Sealed editor reviews use a per-review key held by the vendor; customer-managed keys are not described.

pentest.note: No penetration test statement on the compliance page, privacy policy, DPA or llms.txt.

evidence.quote: Found a vulnerability, or need a Data Processing Agreement

vuln_disclosure.note: The compliance page gives a reporting address (team@kahubi.com) but no disclosure policy or bug bounty. kahubi.com/.well-known/security.txt redirects to localhost:3000 (checked 2026-11-17), so no security.txt is served.

incidents.note: Vendor pages checked: none. WebSearch 2026-11-17 for Kahubi / Avidemic AB breach, IMY or incident returned only unrelated cases (e.g. Miljödata).

status_page.note: No status page linked from the homepage or footer; kahubi.com/status returns 404.

sso.note: The login page shows email and password only. No SAML, OIDC, Google or Microsoft sign-in is named on the pricing, compliance, terms pages or llms.txt.

federation.note: No eduGAIN or national federation membership on vendor pages; web search found no Kahubi entry.

mfa.note: No multi-factor statement on public pages; the login page shows email and password only.

admin_console.note: llms.txt says institutional licences have a seat limit 'managed by a named licence admin at the customer', and team owners can suspend or remove members (terms section 6). No admin console or usage reports are described.

lms_integration.note: No LTI or named LMS (Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard, Brightspace, itslearning) on the homepage, educators page, integrations page or llms.txt.

evidence.quote: Universities evaluating Kahubi can request our current conformance documentation through the same address.

vpat.note: The page does not name a VPAT or ACR; it offers 'conformance documentation' on request.
